The grace of God will deal gently with you; for when it exceeds the limit, it will expose you to disgrace.

In these politically clouded and murky circumstances, where a great many defenseless, grieving, and oppressed citizens are struggling with serious livelihood problems and dire economic conditions, how heartbreaking it is to witness the tragic and shocking situation of someone in your own country. An individual who belongs to the royal family of our country and is presumably meant to be concerned with the soil and the territorial integrity of his homeland; yet he supports the aggression of two countries, America and Israel, against his homeland in two wars of twelve days and forty days, offers condolences for the killing of American soldiers, but refrains from expressing sympathy with the bereaved and afflicted families during these two devastating wars, including the grieving families of the "Shajarat Tayyebeh" school in the city of Minab, and then tries to smooth over this strange behavior of his and offers a justification that only adds to the ugliness of his initial act. Let us pass over the fact that he does not dare say a word thinner than a flower to the criminal prime minister who has sent a number of his innocent compatriots to dust and blood... Furthermore, after his wishes and plans failed and did not come to fruition in the two recent wars, out of anger and desperation in an interview with "Fox News," he implicitly and explicitly spoke of arming the people of his country using Iran's blocked assets held by the American government, and defended it, without pausing for a moment to think that if this brilliant proposal succeeds, its outcome would be heading toward civil war and becoming like Syria, and nothing else; an outcome that has no relation whatsoever to Iranophilia and patriotism!!

When I review the free fall of the son of the last Shah of Iran over the past fifteen months, I am reminded of this profound expression of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of "Matthew": "What profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world, but loses his own soul?" Suppose this anti-Iran and anti-homeland plan mentioned succeeds, whose probability in the current political atmosphere is fortunately low; then what is gained and what does he gain? What profit is it that someone loses human dignity, principles, and moral values, sends his defenseless compatriots to the jaws of death so that he may reach his long-held dream, his unfulfilled regrets may be realized, and he may climb the ladder of power and set up a tent and encampment for himself? Are such relentless and ceaseless struggles, these heart-rending swings to left and right, and the trampling underfoot of numerous moral and human principles — which by the way provide the opportunity for heavy suppression of desperate and afflicted compatriots inside the country — not pitiful and instructive?!

It is fitting that blood should surge in the heart of the ruby-colored mine, for the pottery shard is breaking its market.

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] The whisper of 12. The autumn season has arrived; an autumn that breathes with…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

The whisper of 12. The autumn season has arrived; an autumn that breathes with the blowing of its winds and the turning of its trees' leaves from green to yellow. The month of Mehr is bound to the name and memory of three luminous stars in the sky of Iranian culture and art; cherished souls whose long and deep companionship over the past three decades has polished my soul and gladdened my days: Hafez Shirazi, Sohrab Sepehri, and Mohammadreza Shajarian. Shajarian and Sepehri were born in the month of Mehr. The anniversary commemorating the thinking recluse of Shiraz also falls in this month. I am glad that the lecture series "In the Presence of Hafez" begins the day after tomorrow, in the month of Mehr. In this lecture series, I intend to offer my own re-reading and re-creation of thirty ghazals from the Divan of Hafez and to narrate my roughly forty years of familiarity and intimacy with Hafez's life-world here and now. The opening verse of the first ghazal I have chosen for re-reading and narrative-making is as follows: "If the Sufi drinks wine in measure, may it be sweet to him / Otherwise, may he forget the thought of this affair." Other exquisite verses are also found in this ghazal: "Our elder said no error befell the pen of creation / Bravo to his pure vision that covers errors!" and "The King of Turks listens to the words of claimants / May he be ashamed of the injustice done to the sweet Siyavash!" I have repeatedly read the verses of this stunning artistic work of Hafez over the past decades and have gazed upon them and into them. In this process and in the long future ahead, it is as though both I was reading the ghazal and the ghazal was reading me. For this reason, my present understanding of "pure vision that covers errors" and "shame from the injustice of Siyavash's blood" has noticeably changed. This epistemic transformation can also be explained in the language of Gadamerian hermeneutics and by borrowing the doctrine of the "fusion of horizons." It is obvious that Khwajeh Shams al-Din Mohammad Hafez composed his ghazals seven hundred years ago and read his story into the ear of history. You and I, who are today the audience of these poems, belong to a different context, time, and historical horizon. But this does not prevent the important matter that we strive to the best of our ability, in the light of our lived experience here and now, to become the "audience" of these poems and to understand them; an address that takes place in today's horizon and is the product of our creative and methodical encounter with the text. Of course, in this kind of dialectical encounter with the text, the beliefs, values, attitudes, and the "soul" and "world" of you and me, which have changed over time, pour forth, play an important role in the "process" of addressing the text, and create novel "products" and place them before others." Quoted from the book: "Velvety Whispers," Volume Two. Author: Soroush Dabbagh https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdrpVwpKf7D/?stkn=MmJlbnc2dGV1d284

From afar, I kiss your hands, I am grateful to you, and in the words of Hafez I say to you:

"Never will your image fade from the tablet of my heart and soul
Never will that graceful cypress depart from my memory"

And:
"Upon this turquoise arc they have written in gold

Secondly, I am truly delighted that my oral works and lecture series have been of use to you in these difficult times and that you have found them beneficial. You can download the audio files of the aforementioned lecture series and possibly my other lecture series through my website and Telegram channel, the links of which I am providing for you. Fortunately, the technical work on my latest book and spiritual child, "Narratives of Suffering and War," is nearing completion. I hope it will be published in the first half of Mehr and made available to those interested. Passages from the book's introduction are as follows: "Over the past fifteen months, tremendous and strange events have befallen this land and nation; events the likes of even one of which many people living in Europe, Australia, and North America do not experience in their lifetime. Two devastating wars that began with the blatant aggression of Israel and America against our country's soil, and whose aftershocks are still ongoing and have severely affected the security and livelihood of millions of Iranians. Tragically, more than four thousand of my and your compatriots have been drenched in their own blood during these two wars, including the innocent elementary school students of the 'Shajarat Tayyebah' school in Minab County. In addition, the horrific events that occurred after last Dey's protests and in the interval between the two wars, which took the lives of more than three thousand protesting and desperate citizens and cast their lifeless bodies upon the soil. In the midst of this, many families were bereaved, distraught, and destroyed, and they still remain in shock, mourning, and sorrow. Tragically, the ongoing sorrowful tale of the executions of Dey's protesters has added to the volume of these calamities. The psyche of many citizens has been wounded and afflicted during this period, and their wounds still bleed. The storm of events has made the atmosphere extremely dusty, and many people, with an abundance of fear and worry, are monitoring news filled with ambiguity, hoping that through the thought, judgment, and prudence of a few of the rulers, they might 'tunnel toward the light' and imagine a better future. The writer of these lines, although by the decree of fate has resided in North America for years and spends days and nights in this geographical region; yet his heart and soul are deeply bound to that soil and water and beat with longing for its prosperity and elevation, for 'my lamp burns in this house, my water is drunk from the jug of this Ayaz, and my bread is on this table'... Now that the waters have somewhat settled and the dust has subsided, I give thanks to the soul of the world that in those days when 'stones were raining down from the catapult of the heavens' and a heavy atmosphere prevailed, especially outside the country, and openly opposing the war was not an easy task; I did not become captive to the 'dictatorship of the atmosphere' and was not subjugated by the praise and blame of Amr and Zayd, I did not deviate from my national and ethical principles, and I defended the territorial integrity of Iran and the soil and water and my country. "Never shall your image depart from the tablet of my heart and soul,
Never shall that graceful cypress depart from my memory.
Whatever burden of grief for you rests upon my wretched heart,
It may depart from my heart, but that one shall never depart from my heart."

On the arrival of the fourth anniversary of the passing of the dear Mahsa Amini and all those killed in the progressive and blessed movement "Woman, Life, Freedom" — a movement that, though suppressed, had lasting achievements and imposed itself upon the rulers, forcing them to accept the colorful lifestyles of citizens....

The written account and the collection of my writings during the days of the "Mahsa Movement" have been recorded in a chapter of the book "The Untrodden Path: Essays on Politics, Religion, and Society," read to the ear of history, and placed before audiences and those interested. In hope of the arrival of a bright tomorrow — a tomorrow in which economic and psychological security, freedom, social justice, and fundamental citizenship rights are institutionalized in our beloved country, and our sorrowful and suffering people no longer pass their nights and days and "still" in longing to obtain and taste them:

"Someday we will find our doves again
And kindness will take the hand of beauty
A day when the least song
Is a kiss
And every human being
For every human being
Is a brother...
A day when you come, when you come forever
And kindness becomes one with beauty
A day when we again scatter seeds for our doves, and I await that day
Even a day when I no longer exist"
